situation:
You are a high-school senior who has just cashed a first part-time paycheck from a grocery store, about $520 a month. You live with your mother in a rented apartment, and an apartment two floors down was burglarized last week. The judge is an agent at LAKESIDE MUTUAL INSURANCE.

Your mother has asked you to split the cost of a renter's policy. A $250 deductible costs $22 a month; a $1,000 deductible costs $11 a month. Neither of you has $1,000 on hand, and your mother has covered gaps before with a payday loan from QUICKFUND PAYDAY.

You have saved $2,400 toward your first year of college and expect to borrow the rest in student loans. You know those loans can be deferred while you are enrolled. You have never seen your own file at any of the national credit reporting companies.

The agent (judge) has asked you to recommend which deductible to take and how to pay for it. Paying half of the $22 a month policy takes money out of the $2,400 college savings and slows that goal. Taking the $11 a month policy with the $1,000 deductible leaves your mother owing $1,000 after a break-in, which is what sent her to QUICKFUND PAYDAY before.

The agent (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are an agent at LAKESIDE MUTUAL INSURANCE. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the senior to recommend which deductible the household should carry, how the premium is split against a $520 a month paycheck, and what the choice means for the $2,400 in college savings and for the borrowing that follows it.

During the presentation you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how will this choice have changed what you do in an emergency?
If you defer your student loans after you enroll, what will that cost you later?
